title: Fine-grained attribution normalizer for per-route/model/customer econ
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Build a resilient service that computes cost and latency breakdowns at the granularity of (route, model, customer) by merging streaming inference telemetry with periodic billing events. The service must handle out-of-order or missing KV-cache and batching signals, be tolerant to partial failures, and produce immutable daily materialized views for downstream Console dashboards and chargeback pipelines. Goals: 1) accurate and explainable per-request attribution, 2) predictable latency for the pipeline (bounded windowing), 3) de-duplicated accounting across streamed events and batch rollups, and 4) clear fallback semantics when model variants or quantization metadata are missing.
acceptance_criteria: Daily materialized view available for all production routes with <1% reconciliation drift vs. billing ledger over a 7-day test window
End-to-end pipeline 95th percentile processing lag < 10 minutes for streaming events; daily rollups complete within 30 minutes of window end
Attribution records include provenance (span ids, kernel signature, batching key) so Console can surface explainability for each cost/latency line item
Fallback path defined and implemented for missing model attribute (maps to compatible model variant) with documented effect on reported unit-cost
Automated tests cover event-time joins, duplicates, and late-arrival correction logic; PRs reviewed and approved by both Runtime and Console owners
tasks: Spike: simulate realistic event distributions (KV cache hits, batch sizes, multiple model variants) and measure aggregator accuracy

Design: define canonical schema for attribution records and MV (fields: route, model_hash, model_variant, customer_id, tokens_in, tokens_out, kernel_ms, queue_ms, batch_size, cost_usd, event_time, ingestion_time, provenance)
Implement streaming pipeline (Apache Beam on Flink) for real-time joins and de-duplication with a compact out-of-order buffer
Implement daily batch reconciler that merges streaming MVs with billing events and emits final per-route/model/customer ledger
Add metrics and dashboards for reconciliation drift, duplicate suppression rate, late-arrival correction counts
Integrate output into Console endpoints and ensure RBAC on MV reads for Private deployments
notes: We chose Apache Beam on Flink for portability between cloud managed runners and on-prem installs; trade-off: slightly more operational overhead than a pure Kafka+Flink native stack but better portability for Redwood Private customers.

Probabilistic apportionment: when a request traverses multiple model variants (fallbacks), we allocate latency/cost proportionally to measured kernel_ms and token counts; heuristic validated in spike with synthetic traces.
Storage: use read-optimized materialized views in ClickHouse for Console reads; use RocksDB-backed state for streaming aggregations to lower memory footprint.
Privacy: customer_id is the only PII-like field; outputs will use deterministic pseudonymous mapping for Console unless tenant grants cleartext access (Private deployment exception).

We must avoid double-charging when both streaming path and daily batch include the same invocation — de-duplication is done via a canonical request id + ingestion watermarking window; late-arrivals beyond the retention window are marked for manual review and tracked in a drift dashboard.
